newsitem.title: CANADA: StatsCan study bearish wheat, bullish canola-trade.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan study bearish wheat, bullish canola-trade.

text.p: Statistics Canada's March 31 stocks report issued Tuesday was construed as bearish to wheat futures but bullish for canola and flax, analysts said.
"That's a big wheat number. It's massive at 19.3 million tonnes," XCan Grain Pool Ltd analyst Keith Ferley said.

A record grain crop was harvested last fall but extreme cold and heavy snow along with equipment failure delayed railcar shipments to Pacific ports from January to March and led to a backlog in exports.
StatsCan's survey found 13.935 million tonnes of wheat stored on farm and 5.38 million in commercial facilities.
"The wheat number's larger by about 100,000 tonnes but the barley and oats are right on," LFG analyst Rob Dzisiak said.
StatsCan's survey found 5.825 million tonnes of barley stored on farm and 1.023 million in commercial facilities.
StatsCan's report found 1.425 million tonnes of oats on farm and 0.236 million in commercial facilities.
"My canola number was 60,000 tonnes more and my flax number was 25,000 tonnes more but I don't know if it's that big a deal," Dzisiak said.
StatsCan's survey showed 1.4 million tonnes of canola on farm and 0.625 million in commercial facilities.
StatsCan's report showed 0.285 million tonnes of flax stored on farm and 0.14 million in commercial facilities.

"I was looking for 430,000 tonnes in the flax," ScotiaMcLeod analyst Rob Gigiel said. "There could be a short fall in flax and there's talk the Europeans are looking to buy flax before the (Canadian) dollar rises."
StatsCan said it didn't count about three million acres of unharvested grains and oilseeds in the northwest Prairies.
"I think the report's going to be a non event because people are going to think it's so mixed up," Continental Grain Co Canada analyst Greg Kostal said.
Some analysts assumed 200,000 tonnes of canola in the affected regions could not be salvaged and should not be calculated in future supply and disposition estimates.

"Canola is certainly looking on the snug side," United Grain Growers Ltd analyst Mike Jubinville said. "I expect that at this pace usage will match my projection of 2.575 million tonnes for domestic crush and I wouldn't discount doing more."
Canola exports, however, were about 200,000 tonnes behind last year for the same period, Jubinville said.
"Exports have been slow except for the big business on Friday but there's not a lot of room for new business," he said.
